offences.quote: Any of the below definitions may also include the unauthorised use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) or other mechanisms.
This is presenting work which is not your own, without acknowledgement of the source, as your own work.
This happens if you make up (or manipulate) data or results and record or report on them in a piece of assessment.
This happens if you arrange for an assessment to be completed by a third party and pass the assessment off as your own.
Copying from, or trying to copy from, another candidate
The possession of technological or electronic devices such as mobile phones, smart watches and hidden earpieces/micro earbuds/mini cameras
This happens if you submit a piece of work done in collaboration with another student as if the work was entirely your own.
This happens if you pay; offer some other inducement; or through intimidation attempt to gain an unfair advantage in an assessment.
Submitting the same piece of assessment for two different modules would be self-plagiarism.

detection.quote: The evidence will normally include the Turnitin Report, if this is relevant
we may ask you to attend a further meeting with your Module Leader or Project Supervisor to answer more detailed questions.

process.quote: If your Course Leader and person identifying the misconduct judge that the instance is likely to be a minor one, as set out in the List of Sanctions, we will deal with your case informally.
If your case is considered to be more serious it will be referred to an Academic Conduct Panel.
If your Tutor believes that you have committed academic misconduct, they will gather all evidence and inform your Course Leader.
You will have the opportunity to explain your side and provide us with any evidence you would like us to consider.
Hearings will normally be convened on scheduled dates throughout the academic year, with cases referred to the next available hearing.
you may bring with you a fellow student or representative of the Students’ Union.
If you disagree with the decision made on your Academic Conduct case, you can submit an appeal, although the grounds for doing so are limited.
Appeals must be submitted within two weeks.
We will consider all of the evidence to make a decision based on the balance of probability.

outcomes.quote: If we feel that your work contains poor academic practice, we will discuss this with you and advise you on how you can improve.
outcomes.anchor: How is poor academic practice different?

outcomes.quote: Failure of the assessment. You will be reassessed, should an opportunity exist.
Failure of the module concerned with a right to be reassessed should an opportunity exist.
Failure of the award and/or termination of your studies at the University.
Normally a second or third offence or any instance of contract cheating/impersonation.

definitions.quote: Any action which could give you, or someone else, an unfair advantage in an assessment, including examinations.
Poor academic practice happens when you have used too much of other’s work in your assessment, even when you have acknowledged, and we can’t tell how much you’ve learned for yourself.
This is presenting work which is not your own, without acknowledgement of the source, as your own work.
This happens if you submit a piece of work done in collaboration with another student as if the work was entirely your own.
This happens if you arrange for an assessment to be completed by a third party and pass the assessment off as your own.
This is called a Viva Voce and this is outside of your normal assessment, this means that it will not contribute towards your mark
